tasks.short: Plan collections and exhibitions and develop exhibit materials

steps.what: Plan acquisition, storage and exhibition themes with collection stakeholders
Develop exhibit materials and coordinate physical installation

tasks.design: Keep collection choices, exhibition interpretation and physical installation with the curator. Use {DOCS} for working plans; no separate clerical baseline or automated design decision is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collection meaning and feasible installations depend on objects, context and space.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing documents support planning without changing the work allocation.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing interpretation, conservation, access and contested histories.
tasks.human_edge: The curator takes responsibility for what the exhibition says and how objects are treated.

reach.learn: Understand handling limits before committing to a design

evidence.claim: Keeping collection interpretation and installation manual is an unmeasured task design.

assumptions: The baseline includes planning, material development and installation rather than a separate repetitive publishing operation.
No machine consumes structured object eligibility or installation readiness fields.
Existing document tools suffice; there is no new service to maintain.
No incremental upkeep is introduced because the workflow remains manual.
unknowns: Exhibition scale and repeatability of labels
research_questions: How much time is actually spent repeating previously approved exhibit text?

already_counted.description: Interpretation and installation checks remain in the existing work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; gross and net saving are zero. No measured clerical component supports a reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define registration fields and capture source records for database maintenance
Validate database fields and copy unchanged registration values
Resolve cataloging exceptions and verify database changes

tasks.design: Configure the existing collection database, represented by {OTHER}, for validated imports and required fields. The curator prepares the mapping and source batch, and resolves every exception before saving catalogue changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated copying between lists and the collection database.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import mappings and field validation can remove repeated transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain provenance and ambiguous object descriptions require research.
tasks.human_edge: The curator defines the record's meaning and decides whether evidence warrants a change.

reach.learn: Use stable identifiers and distinguish evidence from interpretation

evidence.claim: Configured database imports and validation are a proposed deterministic approach, not a measured curator deployment.

assumptions: This task concerns system maintenance; substantive new descriptions and acquisition appraisal are outside the saving.

The curator produces object identifier, source reference, target field, value, mapping version and allowed-value rules in s1; its 35 hours include capture and correction. Missing mappings stay manual in s3.
Use native collection database imports before custom integration; OTHER means collection database.
Thirty-five copied hours are a hypothesis; ongoing rule maintenance is additional.
research_questions: Can a representative import preserve identifiers and expose all unmapped values without changing source meaning?

already_counted.description: Source capture, mapping and exception verification

incremental.description: Maintain mappings and sample import integrity

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=65 gives 35 gross, less 8 focal upkeep gives 27 central net. Report only 0-7 while copied-field prevalence and native configuration are untested; low case already has imports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct specialist collection research

steps.what: Plan research questions and examine original collection evidence
Evaluate findings and conduct specialist research discussions

tasks.design: Retain specialist research and source interpretation as human work, using {DOCS} for notes. Do not treat searchable records as proof of provenance or reserve an invented drafting stage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research depends on incomplete and contested primary evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and note tools assist access without replacing interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Judging authenticity, historical context and unresolved contradictions.
tasks.human_edge: The curator can defend a qualified conclusion and identify what remains unknown.

evidence.claim: Searchable historical transcriptions can remain uncorrected and contain errors; this does not establish research labour savings.

assumptions: The baseline is original research rather than mass handwriting transcription.
The curator produces source notes and findings in s1; expert responses are obtained through s2 discussions, with all time retained.
Existing documents and catalogue search suffice before building any research assistant.
There is no new automated service or incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Does transcription consume a measurable share of these research projects?

already_counted.description: Primary evidence assessment and expert discussion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. Searchability evidence does not measure this specialist research task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify information requests and select releasable holdings records
Draft information answers with holdings references

loop.purpose: Draft a response from selected catalogue evidence
loop.input: Question brief and releasable source packet
loop.output: Draft with record identifiers and quoted supporting fields
loop.check: Resolve every identifier and have the curator compare each assertion with the underlying record
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing or contradictory support returns to manual answering
loop.why_not_simpler: Literal catalogue links suffice for simple requests; prose synthesis across records requires language interpretation

steps.what: Verify holdings information and send the approved answer

tasks.design: Use native catalogue links first and an assistant over selected records in the collection database {OTHER} for synthesis. The curator checks assertions and access restrictions and sends the final answer through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated prose responses require gathering and explaining several catalogue records.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference assistants can produce source-linked drafts, while deterministic identifier checks reject nonexistent records.
tasks.still_hard: A real record can still be misinterpreted or restricted.
tasks.human_edge: The curator judges context, uncertainty and what can be shared.

reach.learn: Separate record retrieval from substantiating an answer

evidence.claim: Primo Research Assistant produces reference answers from the top five abstracts with source links; this supports a capability analogy, not curator savings.
The proposed curator workflow and time allowances are unmeasured.

assumptions: Public request answering is separate from maintaining the underlying catalogue.
The curator produces question scope, record identifiers, source excerpts and release decisions in s1; 35 hours include capture. Missing access decisions or sources force manual answering.
Native catalogue search and reusable approved responses precede a model loop; OTHER means collection database.
No automatic external answer is permitted.
research_questions: Do checked multi-record drafts reduce total answering time without unsupported claims or disclosure errors?

already_counted.description: Request capture, draft checking and final release

incremental.description: Maintain approved source scope and review failed answers
Maintain access filters and reference checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact answer text, recipient and supporting records; changes require another curator review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=89.5 gives 10.5 gross less 5 focal upkeep =5.5 central net. Report 0-2 until mixed requests are timed; simple links may already suffice and hard questions may need complete rewriting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Interpret and safeguard collections while improving record handling
reach: Work with technicians on installation constraints
role.ambitious_version: A curator who makes holdings easier to access while retaining responsibility for meaning and provenance
